scope: 2020-2026. 2026 from ESPN transactions; 2020-2025 rebuilt from weekly roster snapshots (player-for-player trades only).

meta.source: Flaim Fantasy (ESPN): get_transactions (trade, trade_proposal, trade_decline, trade_veto, trade_uphold), get_roster week snapshots, get_draft 2026, get_matchups player detail weeks 4-7

coverage.2026: weeks 0-8, every trade lifecycle type; truncated=false on every call
coverage.2020-2025: player trades rebuilt from weekly roster snapshots; see league-trades-history.json meta.method

method: ESPN's structured feed leaves out player sides on accepted trade rows (structured_details_incomplete). Sides were rebuilt by diffing weekly roster snapshots and cross-checked against current rosters where acquisitionType is TRADE. All 14 TRADE-tagged players are accounted for.
Duplicate proposal rows (the same offer logged twice within days) are deduped; rawProposalRows keeps the original count.

trade_veto rows give one team id per row. ESPN does not say whether that is the voter, so these are labelled veto votes logged. Every trade that drew veto rows still went through, except possibly the unmatched accept rows.
Display names follow league-h2h-history.json (teamIndex and seasonNames aliases). Raw ESPN team names are not stored.

2026-10-31: Josh Jacobs' Thursday week-8 total (23.2, full PPR, started) was added to trade 2026-T6 only. The value verdict was not recomputed. Pending offers are not stored on accepted trades and are never rendered.
meta.gradingMethod: Trades are graded on long-term value, not starters. For each player we count every point he scored for his new fantasy team after the trade, benched or started, through week 7 (the last completed week). We compare his points per game in games actually played before the trade with after it, using ESPN game logs and schedules so byes and injury absences are labelled and kept out of per-game rates. Rest-of-season value comes from FantasyCalc redraft values (10 teams, 1QB, full PPR to match the league). FantasyCalc publishes only current values, so value at the trade date is approximated from its 30-day trend only for the Sep 28 trades. The later trades use the per-game trend instead. Each side gets paying off, even or backfiring from the current value edge (±10% band) and the points gained (±10 band). When the two conflict, value wins. Confidence scales with the weeks of post-trade data.

pastSeasons.source: Flaim Fantasy (ESPN) get_matchups detail=players for each matchup in weeks 1-13 (2020) / 1-14 (2021-2025); ESPN public players_wl for positions.
pastSeasons.whyNotTransactions: ESPN transactions for past seasons are unavailable: Flaim get_transactions returns ESPN_SEASON_NOT_SUPPORTED, and ESPN direct API returns 401 AUTH_LEAGUE_NOT_VISIBLE (private league, needs login cookies, which were not used).
method: A trade is inferred when players move directly between the same two teams in both directions between consecutive weekly roster snapshots.
Player-for-pick or one-way deals cannot be told apart from waiver pickups and are not listed. Draft-day/offseason trades are not visible either.
If a player was traded and then dropped or traded again before the next weekly snapshot he would be missed.
Kicker/defense-only swaps on both sides are treated as waiver churn and excluded (see excludedLikelyWaiverChurn).
nflTeam is the player NFL team at the end of that season per ESPN, not necessarily at trade time.
pastSeasons.grading: Points the received players scored for the new team (all roster spots) from the first week after the trade through the end of that regular season. Edge under 10 points = even; 75+ = lopsided. No long-term value.
